mission: Decide whether we should migrate our product-analytics workload from Postgres to ClickHouse, or whether a cheaper option meets our needs. The real goal is dashboards that are fast enough for the business at acceptable cost and operational risk. Assumed intention: we have not committed to migrating; if the evidence clearly favors migration, say so and stop at a recommendation rather than writing a migration plan.
provisions:
[PASTE: table sizes, row counts, growth rate] [PASTE: slowest queries with latency and frequency]
- Team: [N] engineers; no one has run ClickHouse in production. - Dashboard latency target: [TARGET, e.g. p95 under N seconds] (state an assumption if this is blank). - Budget/ops constraints: [ANY KNOWN LIMITS].
order_of_operations: 1. State the decision criteria and their weights before evaluating any option. 2. Evaluate at least three options against those criteria: (a) Postgres with targeted tuning (indexes, partitioning, materialized views or rollups), (b) Postgres plus a columnar extension or read replica, (c) ClickHouse. 3. Recommend one option, with the conditions under which the recommendation flips. 4. Propose the single cheapest experiment that would most reduce uncertainty.
scope: - Base claims on the pasted data; label any figure you estimate as an estimate. - Include migration and operational costs, not only query speed. - If the data is insufficient for a confident recommendation, say what is missing.
success_spec: Output: a decision memo in Markdown, under 700 words, with sections: Recommendation (one sentence) · Criteria and weights · Option comparison (table) · Risks · What would change this decision · Next experiment · Confidence (high/medium/low, with one-line reason). Before returning, check: the criteria section precedes the comparison; every non-pasted number is labelled as an estimate; the recommendation is consistent with the comparison table.
